# LokalBot

> Your personal context engine. LokalBot is a free, open-source (GPLv3) app for macOS, with Windows and Linux in alpha, that records meetings without a bot, transcribes and summarizes them on-device, and searches your meetings and, if you turn it on, what you saw on screen. Processing runs locally by default, with no account, analytics, or hosted AI service. Full benchmark tables, comparisons, and FAQs in one file: https://www.lokalbot.com/llms-full.txt

Key facts:

- Platforms: macOS 15.0 or later on Apple Silicon (M1 or later). In alpha: Windows 10 or 11 (x64) and Linux (x86_64, glibc 2.39 or later), a separate native app that reads the same library format. An Android companion app (Android 10 or later) is on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=me.dotenv.lokalbot.companion. No Intel Mac or web version, and the iPhone and iPad app isn't in the App Store yet.
- Price and license: free, GNU GPL v3; code in the Autocomplete engine that was ported from Cotabby stays under AGPLv3. Source: https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot
- Install: from https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest download LokalBot-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg (or run `brew install --cask stevyhacker/tap/lokalbot`) on a Mac, LokalBot-<version>-windows-x86_64-setup.exe (a per-user installer) or the portable LokalBot-<version>-windows-x86_64.zip on Windows (neither code-signed yet), or LokalBot-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz (or the .deb, .rpm or Arch package from the same release) on Linux (for the archive, run ./install.sh). The .deb, and the .rpm on Fedora, add the LokalBot repository at pkg.lokalbot.com, so apt or dnf keeps it updated.
- Phones and tablets: the Android app pairs by QR code with LokalBot on a Mac, Windows, or Linux computer (Settings → Phones & tablets, off by default). It keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of the meetings, actions, Timeline, Day Digests, people, and projects the user chooses to share, syncs directly over the local network or Tailscale with no LokalBot server, searches that copy offline, and sends Ask questions to the computer, which answers with its own AI settings.
- Meetings: records the microphone and the meeting app's audio on separate tracks without joining the call (on Windows and Linux, the meeting app where it can be separated, and otherwise everything the computer plays). On a fresh install it asks through a notification before recording a detected meeting.
- Local models: on Mac, Qwen3-ASR 1.7B is the default speech model (since 0.8.1); Parakeet, IBM Granite Speech, and Whisper large-v3 turbo are alternatives. On Windows and Linux the default is Qwen3-ASR 0.6B, with Parakeet, SenseVoice, GigaAM for Russian, and Whisper turbo. Summaries use Qwen3.5 4B on llama.cpp and search uses EmbeddingGemma 2 embeddings everywhere. On Windows and Linux, llama.cpp runs on a Vulkan GPU, the CPU, or an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA (experimental). Speakers you name are recognized in later meetings; on Windows and Linux the name is only offered for the user to apply.
- Optional backends: Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers, and the user's ChatGPT or Claude plan on every platform, plus Apple Intelligence on Mac (macOS 26+). A non-local server or plan must be explicitly approved before it receives meeting or workday context.
- Languages: Qwen3-ASR transcribes 52 languages and dialects; meeting notes follow the meeting's language unless the user picks another; the interface is translated into 24 languages.
- Workday memory: day tracking starts with app names and window titles only. Saved screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in; screenshots are deleted after 14 days by default.
- Also includes: hold-to-talk dictation (⌥ Space on Mac, Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) with recent dictations kept to copy again, optional local autocomplete that can use the message being answered and the user's meetings, a sample meeting to try before recording, import of audio and video files as meetings, a morning look back at yesterday from the overnight review, a Raycast extension (https://www.raycast.com/stevan_bogosavljevic/lokalbot), an open-source Obsidian plugin (https://github.com/stevyhacker/obsidian-lokalbot), selection actions for rewriting selected text, spoken summaries, search across folders the user chooses, Markdown/Obsidian/Logseq export, a read-only CLI and MCP server that stay off until the user turns them on in Settings, opening a meeting's action item in Claude Code or Codex, and opt-in Agent Mode, which works on files with approval and can run on a ChatGPT plan.
- Projects: tracks a project by name and gathers the meetings, actions, and decisions that name it, writes a short "Where it stands" note with links back to its meetings, and suggests names that keep coming up.
- Mainland China: records Tencent Meeting, VooV Meeting, Feishu, Lark, DingTalk, and WeCom calls; keyword search matches Chinese, Japanese, and Korean anywhere in a phrase; models can download from HF-Mirror or ModelScope instead of Hugging Face (Settings → Models).
- Personal Context: an encrypted list of facts, preferences, goals, and principles about the user, from "Remember …" in Ask, items added in Settings, and what it learns overnight from the user's own words in meetings and typed requests. Ask uses it; agents can read only items the user shares, under a separate permission.
- Mac only for now: Gmail in meeting briefs, Apple Intelligence, Granite Speech transcription, and Nemotron speaker separation.
- Limits on Windows and Linux: on Linux, autocomplete in other apps works on X11 and, as an input method on Wayland, on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma (lightly tested so far), but not yet on other compositors; dictation and selection actions on Wayland need a desktop shortcut; reading screen text in scripts other than Latin needs Tesseract on Linux; remembered speakers are only suggestions the user applies; Files doesn't read .doc, RAW, or some scanned PDF pages, and video frames, HEIC, and AVIF need ffmpeg.
- Not supported: syncing a library between computers or through a cloud service.

## Product

- [LokalBot home](https://www.lokalbot.com/): features, demo, and FAQ
- [Agent Wrapped](https://www.lokalbot.com/wrapped): local, zero-upload year in review for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, OMP, OpenCode, Antigravity, and Gemini CLI (`npx lokalbot`)
- [Meeting Migrator](https://www.lokalbot.com/migrate): offline, zero-upload browser converter that turns Granola, Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, and Zoom meeting exports into Obsidian Markdown notes with YAML frontmatter, speaker wikilinks, and a ZIP download
- [Local AI Hardware & RAM Calculator](https://www.lokalbot.com/hardware): interactive zero-upload browser calculator for Apple Silicon Macs, Windows, and Linux estimating exact disk downloads, resident RAM, KV-cache allowances, GPU VRAM offload, and LokalBot's 50% memory residency cap
- [About LokalBot](https://www.lokalbot.com/about): fact sheet, what it does and does not do
- [System requirements](https://www.lokalbot.com/system-requirements): Mac, Windows, and Linux requirements, memory, disk, permissions, and what each platform supports
- [Local Desktop AI Leaderboard](https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks): interactive, reproducible benchmarks across 7 workloads and 17 suites (speech vs. cloud APIs, diarization, memory recall vs. restraint, 56 ms autocomplete, hybrid QMSum retrieval, extraction, OCR, TTS) with machine-readable JSON at [benchmarks.json](https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks.json)
- [Privacy policy](https://www.lokalbot.com/privacy): what stays on your computer and exactly when the app uses the network

## Blog

- [LokalBot blog](https://www.lokalbot.com/blog): releases, local model benchmarks, and build notes ([Atom feed](https://www.lokalbot.com/blog/feed.xml))
- [39 ms and 50 MB vs. 255 ms and 1 GB: QMSum local retrieval benchmark](https://www.lokalbot.com/blog/gbrain-vs-lokalbot-memory-benchmark): LokalBot's SQLite FTS5 + EmbeddingGemma 2 retrieval vs. GBrain across 232 public meetings and 1,576 questions
- [Local speech-to-text vs. cloud APIs on real meetings](https://www.lokalbot.com/blog/local-stt-vs-cloud-apis): Qwen3-ASR 1.7B and Parakeet local vs. Gemini 3.5/3.8, GPT-4o Transcribe, GPT Transcribe, and Qwen-Audio on AMI and two-track calls
- [56 ms local system-wide autocomplete benchmark](https://www.lokalbot.com/blog/local-autocomplete-56ms-benchmark): headless keystroke benchmark of Gemma 4 E2B vs. LFM2.5 1.2B across 788 word positions
- [Recall vs. restraint](https://www.lokalbot.com/blog/recall-vs-restraint-memory-benchmark): a 120-case benchmark of local models deciding what to save as a memory and what to leave out
- [LokalBot is on Windows and Linux, in alpha](https://www.lokalbot.com/blog/windows-and-linux-alpha): what works, what is missing, default models, and installation
- [How the Windows and Linux port was built](https://www.lokalbot.com/blog/porting-to-windows-and-linux-with-agents): specs first, how coding agents' work was checked, and a link to the full write-up

## Full Benchmark Dataset (https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks · updated 2026-11-20)

Primary desktop runs on Apple M4 Max (48 GB unified memory); Linux CPU memory/extraction runs on AMD Ryzen 7 9700X (64 GB); experimental MemT run on Windows + RX 6600 XT.

### Current local reference stack

| Role | Default model | Format | Size (GB) | Headline |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Transcription | Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | MLX 8-bit / GGUF Q8_0 | 2.47 | 17.6% WER · 44× RT |
| Speaker Diarization | Nemotron 3 | Core ML (FluidAudio) | 0.2 | 14.56% DER · 500× RT |
| Hybrid Search | EmbeddingGemma 2 | GGUF Q8_0 + SQLite FTS5 | 0.31 | 39 ms p50 · 50 MB RAM |
| Inline Autocomplete | Gemma 4 E2B Base | GGUF i1-Q6_K (llama.cpp) | 3.85 | 56 ms · 50.1% precision |
| Summaries & Memory | Qwen3.5 4B | GGUF Q4_K_M (llama.cpp) | 2.74 | 33.4 s warm · 95.5% restraint |
| Screen OCR & Voice | Apple Vision + Kokoro 82M | macOS native + local TTS | 0.1 | 0.971 F1 · 119.6 ms OCR |

### Speech-to-Text (Meetings, Multilingual & Live)

Local ASR models measured head-to-head against OpenAI, Google, and Alibaba cloud STT APIs on overlapped AMI meetings, real two-track calls, multilingual FLEURS clips, and turn-by-turn live latency.

#### AMI Meetings: Local ASR vs. Closed Cloud APIs (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#stt-ami-cloud`)
- Run date: 2026-09-30 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · MLX 0.32.3 / mlx-audio 0.5.7 · direct cloud APIs
- Dataset: 16 windows (90–120 s) from 4 AMI Mix-Headset test meetings · 27.4 min · 4,160 reference words
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/transcribe/CloudSTT/results/2026-09-30/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | AMI WER ↓ | 95% CI | Low-overlap ↓ | Speed ↑ | Price / hr ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash (prompted) | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 16.7% | 14.0–19.0% | 6.2% | 18× | $0.21 |
| Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | default | MLX 8-bit · 8-bit · 2.47 GB | 17.6% | 14.6–20.5% | 7.1% | 44× | $0 |
| Qwen3-ASR Flash | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 18.1% | 14.6–20.8% | 6.3% | 25× | $0.13 |
| Qwen-Audio 3.1 ASR Flash | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 18.5% | 14.6–21.8% | 5.6% | 10× | $0.02 |
| Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 | option | MLX / Core ML · 0.63 GB | 19.2% | 15.8–22.3% | 8.1% | 129× | $0 |
| GPT-4o mini Transcribe | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 21.8% | 17.5–25.7% | 7.8% | 34× | $0.18 |
| GPT Transcribe | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 22.2% | 17.6–27.5% | 6.9% | 30× | $0.27 |
| GPT-4o Transcribe | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 23.0% | 18.4–27.0% | 6.2% | 25× | $0.36 |

Note: Heavy overlapped crosstalk on a single mixed channel makes deletions dominate every system's WER. Local models run serially with zero upload; API speed includes network upload with 4 requests in flight.
Caveat: Gemini 3.8 Flash edged Qwen3-ASR 1.7B by 0.9 pts on AMI (within CI), but invented 115 words across 15 spans on real quiet meeting chunks (see Real 2-Track Meetings suite).

#### Real Two-Track Meetings: Consensus Disagreement & Hallucinations (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#stt-meetings-agreement`)
- Run date: 2026-09-30 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · MLX local vs direct cloud APIs
- Dataset: 3 real two-track meetings · 99 shared chunks · 69.9 min (no human reference; scored via leave-one-family-out ROVER vote)
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/transcribe/CloudSTT/results/2026-09-30/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | Disagreement ↓ | Invented words ↓ | Dropped words ↓ | Median latency ↓ | Price / hr ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | default | MLX 8-bit · 2.47 GB | 4.2% | 23 | 0 | 0.4 s | $0 |
| Gemini 3.5 Transcribe | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 4.5% | 21 | 11 | 6.3 s | $0.30 |
| Qwen-Audio 3.1 ASR Flash | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 4.6% | 21 | 11 | 2.9 s | $0.01 |
| Qwen3-ASR Flash | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 5.3% | 26 | 12 | 1.3 s | $0.13 |
| GPT Transcribe | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 5.9% | 9 | 37 | 1.2 s | $0.27 |
| GPT-4o mini Transcribe | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 6.2% | 14 | 23 | 1.4 s | $0.18 |
| Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 | option | MLX / Core ML · 0.63 GB | 6.2% | 16 | 83 | 0.2 s | $0 |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash (prompted) | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 7.2% | 115 | 0 | 3.6 s | $0.33 |
| GPT-4o Transcribe | cloud | Cloud API · Hosted | 10.0% | 0 | 278 | 1.3 s | $0.36 |

Note: Measures agreement with independent vendor families, not ground-truth WER. Invented = inserted runs ≥ 4 words; Dropped = deleted runs ≥ 4 words.
Caveat: Reveals failure modes invisible in clean benchmarks: Gemini 3.8 Flash invented 115 words on short/quiet chunks, and GPT-4o Transcribe dropped 278 words on the microphone track.

#### Qwen3-ASR 1.7B Runtime Parity: llama.cpp v1.0.0 vs. MLX (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#stt-llamacpp-vs-mlx`)
- Run date: 2026-11-14 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · macOS 27.2.1 · identical Silero VAD windows
- Dataset: 11 conditions · 6.6 hours of audio (AMI, owner meetings, German/Japanese/Russian/Serbian FLEURS)
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/transcribe/QwenLlamaCpp/results/2026-11-14-llama-v1/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | AMI WER ↓ | German FLEURS ↓ | Serbian + vocab ↓ | EN Speed ↑ | Peak Footprint ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (llama.cpp v1.0.0) | default | llama-server b12359 · Q8_0 + mmproj Q8_0 | 17.76% | 3.9% | 12.4% | 42.2× | 2.35 GB |
| Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (MLX) | baseline | MLX 0.32.3 · 8-bit MLX | 17.80% | 4.5% | 13.4% | 47.2× | 7.60 GB |

Note: Compares ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-GGUF Q8_0 on llama.cpp v1.0.0 (b12359) against aufklarer/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-MLX-8bit on speech-swift 0.0.29.
Caveat: llama.cpp matched or slightly beat MLX on accuracy while cutting peak memory footprint from 7.6 GB to 2.35 GB, at 8–13% slower throughput.

#### Small Local Speech Engines & Multilingual FLEURS (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#stt-small-engines`)
- Run date: 2026-10-09 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · network blocked by macOS
- Dataset: 44 human-transcribed English clips (24 AMI IHM + 20 FLEURS, 810 words) + 8-clip German/French/Polish FLEURS probes
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/transcribe/WhistleComparison/results/2026-10-09/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | English WER ↓ | German WER ↓ | Median clip ↓ | Throughput ↑ | Download ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | default | speech-swift / MLX · 8-bit | 7.65% | 2.20% | 157.0 ms | 40.4× | 2.47 GB |
| Parakeet Ultra 0.6B | option | FluidAudio 0.17.5 Core ML · Core ML | 8.89% | 1.65% | 48.0 ms | 135.6× | 632 MB |
| Whistle (native C++) | rejected | C API · 16.9 MB | 20.25% | 19.78% | 31.7 ms | 200.2× | 16.9 MB |

Note: Bounded evaluation testing whether a 17 MB ultra-small C++ engine (Whistle) could rival Parakeet Ultra or Qwen3-ASR 1.7B.
Caveat: German/French/Polish subsets have 8 clips each (~140–227 words); treat as directional rather than population rankings.

#### Turn-by-Turn Live Transcript Latency (Two-Track Call) (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#stt-live-turns`)
- Run date: 2026-11-10 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · macOS 27.2 · Release build
- Dataset: Scripted two-track English call (25 speaker hand-overs); turn closed at speech pause via Silero VAD
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/transcribe/LiveTurns/results/2026-11-10/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | Turn median ↓ | Turn worst ↓ | Old window median | Turn WER ↓ | Decode only ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Granite Speech 5 fast | option | Core ML / fast EN · English-only | 0.48 s | 0.79 s | 1.74 s | 11.2% | 0.02 s |
| Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 | option | FluidAudio Core ML · 0.63 GB | 0.50 s | 0.81 s | 1.86 s | 3.4% | 0.04 s |
| Parakeet Ultra 0.6B | option | FluidAudio Core ML · 0.63 GB | 0.50 s | 0.81 s | 2.23 s | 4.7% | 0.04 s |
| Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | default | MLX 8-bit · 2.47 GB | 0.64 s | 0.86 s | 1.89 s | 2.9% | 0.15 s |
| Whisper large-v3 turbo | option | WhisperKit 1.1.1 · 1.6 GB | 1.32 s | 1.52 s | 3.22 s | 5.8% | 0.81 s |

Note: Times measure end-of-word to displayed text. Cutting tracks at pauses cut both latency and word errors versus fixed 4–12 s preview windows.
Caveat: Synthetic voices on a scripted call without crosstalk; real meetings have pauses mid-sentence. Muse Voice Transcribe (cloud) measured 0.74 s median on separate AMI audio.

### Speaker Diarization (Who Spoke When)

Four independent English AMI meetings scored both as headset mixes and distant-microphone rooms (8 conditions, 184.55 minutes, 4 speakers each), with overlap scored and no speaker-count hints.

#### AMI Speaker Diarization: Local Core ML vs. Pyannote & Cloud API (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#diarization-ami`)
- Run date: 2026-09-23 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · FluidAudio Core ML · Meta cloud API tested 2026-10-27
- Dataset: 4 English AMI test meetings × 2 mic conditions = 8 recordings · 184.55 min · 4 speakers · overlap scored
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/transcribe/NemotronDiarization/results/2026-09-23/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | DER (0 ms collar) ↓ | DER (250 ms) ↓ | Speaker count ↑ | Speed ↑ | Peak RSS ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Nemotron 3 fast128 | option | Core ML (FluidAudio) · Full precision | 14.51% | 8.19% | 8/8 | 365× | 0.64 GiB |
| Nemotron 3 offline | default | Core ML (FluidAudio) · Full precision · ~0.20 GB | 14.56% | 8.34% | 8/8 | 500× | 0.67 GiB |
| Nemotron 3 c128 W8A8 | option | Core ML (CPU/ANE) · W8A8 | 15.73% | 9.34% | 7/8 | 480× | 0.63 GiB |
| Pyannote Community-1 | option | Core ML (FluidAudio) · Previous default | 43.44% | 30.45% | 5/8 | 243× | 0.68 GiB |
| Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0 | cloud | Cloud realtime API · Hosted ($0.36/hr) | 60.4% | — | 5/8 | Live (0.74 s) | Cloud |

Note: Diarization Error Rate (DER) = missed speech + false alarms + speaker confusion. Speed is warm median on the 17.49-min ES2004a headset recording.
Caveat: Pyannote baseline is the pinned FluidAudio port, not every Pyannote setup. Muse cloud DER (60.4%) includes pauses kept inside turns; cut to reference speech it scored 21.7% vs 11.8% for Nemotron offline.

### Personal Memory Extraction: Recall vs. Restraint

A personal memory writer has two jobs: save durable user facts with valid citations, and return nothing on noise, temporary tasks, third-party gossip, or sensitive exclusions. Most benchmarks only test the first.

#### Recall vs. Restraint — 96 Frozen English Cases (48 Paired Toggles) (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#memory-english`)
- Run date: 2026-10-25 · Hardware: Ryzen 7 9700X Ubuntu CPU (llama.cpp) · MemT on Windows RX 6600 XT (experimental NF4 offload)
- Dataset: 96 frozen English cases (52 eligible memories, 44 empty cases) · identical prompt, JSON schema, greedy seed 0
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/think/MemoryRetention/2026-10-23/memt-nano/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | Useful recall ↑ | Unwanted ↓ | Empty correct ↑ | Full contract ↑ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MemT-1.0-Nano | experimental | Transformers NF4 offload · Exp. NF4 experts / BF16 dense | 98.1% | 6 | 88.6% | 89/96 |
| Qwen3.5 9B | option | llama.cpp · Q4_K_M | 71.2% | 5 | 90.9% | 77/96 |
| Qwen3.5 4B | default | llama.cpp · Q4_K_M · 2.74 GB | 57.7% | 3 | 95.5% | 72/96 |
| LFM2.5 24B-A2B | rejected | llama.cpp · QAD Q4_0 | 76.9% | 53 | 22.7% | 44/96 |
| Hy-Memory 30B-A3B | rejected | llama.cpp · Official Q4_K_M | 100.0% | 76 | 0.0% | 32/96 |

Note: Recall requires both accurate content AND the exact source-line citation. Always returning empty scores 44/44 empty and 0/52 recall; saving everything scores 52/52 recall and 0/44 empty.
Caveat: MemT-1.0-Nano ran under experimental NF4 expert offload on Transformers (different hardware/precision than GGUF arms) and statelessly, so its latent persistent-memory branch was not exercised. Cases and semantic review were assistant-authored.

#### Exploratory Serbian Slice — 24 Frozen Cases (Latin & Cyrillic) (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#memory-serbian`)
- Run date: 2026-10-25 · Hardware: Ryzen 7 9700X Ubuntu CPU (llama.cpp) · MemT on Windows RX 6600 XT
- Dataset: 24 frozen Serbian cases (13 eligible memories, 11 empty cases; 12 Latin, 12 Cyrillic)
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/think/MemoryRetention/2026-10-23/memt-nano/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | Useful recall ↑ | Unwanted ↓ | Empty correct ↑ | Full contract ↑ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MemT-1.0-Nano | experimental | Transformers NF4 offload · Exp. NF4 / BF16 | 100.0% | 3 | 72.7% | 19/24 |
| Qwen3.5 9B | option | llama.cpp · Q4_K_M | 92.3% | 2 | 81.8% | 9/24 |
| Qwen3.5 4B | default | llama.cpp · Q4_K_M · 2.74 GB | 61.5% | 2 | 90.9% | 10/24 |
| Hy-Memory 30B-A3B | rejected | llama.cpp · Official Q4_K_M | 100.0% | 25 | 0.0% | 4/24 |
| LFM2.5 24B-A2B | rejected | llama.cpp · QAD Q4_0 | 61.5% | 37 | 0.0% | 3/24 |

Note: Checks recall, restraint, and whether models preserve original language and script without silently translating to English.
Caveat: Exploratory slice only. Hy-Memory advertises English and Chinese coverage; 3 of MemT's Serbian outputs switched language or script.

### System-Wide Local Autocomplete (Inline Cotyping)

Headless engine benchmarks measuring per-keystroke latency, safety, confidence-gated precision across 788 word boundaries, and first-suggestion recovery after a 5-minute pause.

#### Production Autocomplete Engine: Gemma 4 E2B vs. LFM2.5 1.2B (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#autocomplete-engine`)
- Run date: 2026-10-15 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · Release build · in-process llama.cpp
- Dataset: 140 safety checks (28 scenarios × 5 passes) + 788 word positions in 96 synthetic phrases across 6 languages
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/autocomplete/Cotyping/results/2026-10-15-engine-benchmark/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | Right when shown ↑ | Next-word acc ↑ | Non-EN acc ↑ | Keystroke p50 ↓ | Unsafe / 140 ↓ | Model size ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Gemma 4 E2B Base | default | In-process llama.cpp · i1-Q6_K · 3.85 GB | 50.1% | 23.1% | 14.6% | 56 ms | 0 | 3.85 GB |
| LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct | option | In-process llama.cpp · Q4_K_M · 0.73 GB | 43.0% | 20.7% | 7.3% | 26 ms | 0 | 0.73 GB |

Note: Accuracy counts held-back suggestions as misses; 'Right when shown' measures precision when the confidence gate displays text. In English, the two models are statistically tied (+1.1 pts, 95% CI −1.4 to +3.5).
Caveat: Engine timings exclude Accessibility field reads and overlay rendering. Synthetic phrases; some confirmed the hybrid decoder before shipping. On Cotabby's separate 782-checkpoint test, Gemma 4 E2B scored 32.7% vs Cotabby's 30.7%.

#### First Suggestion After a 5-Minute Pause (Metal Residency Fix) (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#autocomplete-pause`)
- Run date: 2026-11-18 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · macOS 27.2.1 · llama.cpp v1.0.0 (b12359)
- Dataset: Gemma 4 E2B i1-Q6_K · single keystroke after 300 s idle vs immediate warm reference
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/autocomplete/Cotyping/results/2026-11-18-first-after-pause/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | First suggestion ↓ | Warm reference | Cold penalty ↓ | Wired while idle |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warm-up just before typing (wake / click) | default | llama.cpp v1.0.0 · 1-token touch + seq_rm | 49 ms | 47–49 ms | ~1 ms | Released after 3 min away |
| Warm-up at first keystroke (45 ms debounce) | default | llama.cpp v1.0.0 · 1-token touch + seq_rm | 51.5 ms | 47–49 ms | ~3.5 ms | Released after 3 min away |
| Periodic touch every 60 s while active | option | llama.cpp v1.0.0 · Keep-warm probe | 59 ms | 47 ms | 12 ms | +2–3 GB wired |
| llama.cpp keep-alive raised to 3600 s | rejected | llama.cpp v1.0.0 · Config override | 62 ms | 48 ms | 14 ms | Stays wired 1 hr away |
| Before fix (default 180 s keep-alive) | baseline | llama.cpp v1.0.0 · No warm-up touch | 112.5 ms | 47–49 ms | +47–82 ms | Unwired at 180 s |

Note: After llama.cpp's 180 s GGML_METAL_RESIDENCY_KEEP_ALIVE_S expires, ~3.4 GB of weights unwire (+50–80 ms) and the GPU clocks down (+10–15 ms). Decoding one throwaway token on wake/click/key with llama_synchronize and stripping it via seq_rm preserves the KV prompt.
Caveat: 30-minute pauses under heavy OS memory pressure (file paging) have not been re-measured yet. Four warm-up touches over 5 min added 18 mJ CPU energy (468 vs 450 mJ).

### Local Hybrid Retrieval & Embedding Models

Head-to-head meeting retrieval across 232 public QMSum meetings (1,576 questions) comparing LokalBot's SQLite FTS5 + EmbeddingGemma 2 layer against GBrain v0.60, plus multilingual embedding comparisons.

#### Hybrid Meeting Retrieval: LokalBot (SQLite) vs. GBrain (PGLite MCP) (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#retrieval-qmsum`)
- Run date: 2026-11-17 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · shared EmbeddingGemma 2 Q8_0 server (496 MB peak)
- Dataset: QMSum (232 public meetings, 129,177 turns, 2.1M words, 1,576 specific questions)
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/memory/GBrain/2026-11-17/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | R@1 ↑ | R@4 / R@10 ↑ | MRR ↑ | Query p50 ↓ | RAM ↓ | Context ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| LokalBot Hybrid (FTS5 + EmbeddingGemma 2) | default | SQLite + llama.cpp · RRF k=60 · 167 MB disk | 0.280 | 0.475 | 0.379 | 39 ms | 50 MB | 1.2k ch |
| GBrain v0.60 Keyword-Only | option | PGLite over stdio MCP · Postgres FTS · 185 MB disk | 0.253 | 0.412 | 0.325 | 159 ms | ~1 GB | 97.4k ch |
| GBrain v0.60 Hybrid (EmbeddingGemma 2) | rejected | PGLite + llama.cpp · Conservative mode · 247 MB disk | 0.239 | 0.367 | 0.295 | 255 ms | ~1 GB | 96.8k ch |
| LokalBot Keyword-Only (SQLite FTS5) | baseline | SQLite FTS5 BM25 · 80 MB disk | 0.193 | 0.335 | 0.274 | 3 ms | 50 MB | 718 ch |

Note: Both hybrid configurations queried the exact same EmbeddingGemma 2 Q8_0 llama-server. Cloud Xeon keyword-only repeat matched accuracy exactly.
Caveat: GBrain beat LokalBot in keyword-only mode (2,000-char chunks vs single transcript rows) and ran without a hosted reranker or query expansion. Neither system automatically supersedes unlinked contradictory statements.

#### Multilingual Embedding Models (English + Serbian Latin/Cyrillic) (`https://www.lokalbot.com/benchmarks#retrieval-embeddings`)
- Run date: 2026-10-07 · Hardware: Apple M4 Max (48 GB) · identical llama.cpp build
- Dataset: 48 authored queries (24 English, 24 Serbian/Montenegrin Latin & Cyrillic) across 60 synthetic passages
- Report: https://github.com/stevyhacker/LokalBot/blob/master/Benchmarks/search/EmbeddingGemma2/2026-10-07/REPORT.md

| Model | Status | Runtime / Quant | Top-1 ↑ | Top-5 ↑ | MRR ↑ | Query p50 ↓ | Download ↓ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| EmbeddingGemma 2 | default | llama.cpp · Q8_0 · 768-dim | 89.6% | 100.0% | 0.944 | 9.0 ms | 0.31 GB |
| Harrier 0.6B | baseline | llama.cpp · Q8_0 · 1024-dim | 83.3% | 97.9% | 0.903 | 13.1 ms | 0.64 GB |
| Qwen3-Embedding 0.6B | rejected | llama.cpp · Q8_0 | 72.9% | — | — | — | 0.64 GB |

Note: All models ran at Q8_0 on the same llama.cpp build with their native task prompts.
Caveat: On 48 correlated queries, the +6.3 pt top-1 gain over Harrier is within noise (95% CI −4 to +17 pts); EmbeddingGemma 2 won on matching quality at half the download, half the idle RAM, and 31% lower latency.

Small local LLMs (2B–4B) evaluated on structured action-item extraction (ownership, deadlines, timestamps, Serbian Latin/Cyrillic, prompt injection) and native OpenAI-format tool calling in llama.cpp.

Note: Controlled Linux CPU screen evaluating Apache-2.0 Spark-X2.6-4B as a candidate replacement for Qwen3.5 4B.
Caveat: Linux CPU observations only, not Mac timings. Spark beat Qwen on short extraction (12/12 vs 10/12) but called search_meetings when asked to send email (no email tool exists) and ran 25% slower on ~20K context.

### Screenshot OCR & Local Text-to-Speech

Opt-in on-device screen text extraction (Apple Vision vs. open-source OCR models) and local spoken summary synthesis (Kokoro 82M vs. Breeze TTS 2).

| Apple Vision | default | VNRecognizeTextRequest · 0 MB download | 0.971 | 0.812 | 119.6 ms | 0.971 / 0.971 |
| PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 GGUF | rejected | llama.cpp VLM · GGUF | 0.777 | 0.731 | 1,700 ms | 0.871 / 0.813 |
| DeepSeek-OCR GGUF | rejected | llama.cpp VLM · GGUF | 0.741 | 0.680 | 1,440 ms | 0.844 / 0.732 |

---

## Detailed Competitor Comparisons

### LokalBot vs Granola (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-granola · verified 2026-10-26)

Granola is one of the most polished AI notepads around — bot-free capture, great templates, strong team features, and apps on desktop and phone. The trade-off is that your meetings are processed in the cloud, under an account. LokalBot keeps the bot-free workflow but transcribes and summarizes on your computer by default: no account, no LokalBot backend, and remote inference only when you approve the server.

| Feature | LokalBot | Granola |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where the AI runs | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR speech model by default and llama.cpp summaries | In the cloud, via third-party AI providers |
| Account required | None | Yes |
| Works offline | Fully, after a one-time model download | Needs a connection for AI notes |
| Bot-free meeting capture | Microphone + system audio (just the selected app on Mac; on Windows and Linux, where it can be separated); labels show capture source, not identity | Yes — no bot joins your call |
| Model training on your data | No LokalBot training pipeline or telemetry; approved remote servers have their own terms | Opt-out of model training on every plan |
| Meeting history | Unlimited, stored on your computer | Basic: 30 days · Business and Enterprise: unlimited |
| Compliance | No LokalBot server ever holds your meetings | SOC 2 Type II; HIPAA workspaces on Enterprise |
| Connect AI tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | MCP for Claude, ChatGPT, and others; API on paid plans |
| System-wide dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | No |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping, in almost any app (on Linux: X11, or Wayland on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma) | No |
| Source code | Open source, GPLv3 | Proprietary |
| Price | Free | Basic free · Business $14 per user/mo · Enterprise $35 per user/mo |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; Android companion app | Desktop, iOS, Android, and Apple Watch apps |

- **Q: Isn't bot-free capture the differentiator?** Not anymore — Granola and several others skip the meeting bot now. The differentiator is where processing happens. LokalBot transcribes and summarizes on your computer with its built-in default; if you opt into a remote inference server, it receives the request context.
- **Q: Can I bring my existing Granola notes with me?** Yes. LokalBot imports Granola exports directly into your local library, or you can convert Granola exports into clean Obsidian Markdown offline in your browser with the free Meeting Migrator (zero uploads).
- **Q: What does LokalBot send over the network?** Model downloads, update checks, optional Agent Mode setup, and remote inference origins you explicitly approve. Audio stays on your computer; built-in inference keeps transcript and workday context there too.
- **Q: Can I try LokalBot next to Granola?** Yes. LokalBot is free — run it on your next few meetings and compare the notes. Neither app puts a bot in your call, so nobody on the call will notice either one.

### LokalBot vs Apple Notes (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-apple-notes · verified 2026-10-26)

Why not just use Apple Notes? On macOS 27 it records audio into a note, transcribes it on your Mac, and Apple Intelligence writes a summary — free, with nothing to install. For a voice memo or a lecture, that may be all you need. For meetings, the gap is the other side of the call: Notes records your microphone, so with headphones on it doesn't hear Zoom, Teams, or Meet. LokalBot records the meeting app's audio too, turns each call into notes linked to the discussion, and keeps every meeting searchable on your Mac.

| Feature | LokalBot | Apple Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audio it records | Your microphone + the meeting app's audio, so both sides of a Zoom, Teams, or Meet call are captured | Your microphone only — Notes can't capture what other apps play |
| Starting a recording | Detects meetings and, on a fresh install, asks before recording | You start each recording by hand inside a note |
| Transcription | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR by default, with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | On your Mac, with Apple's speech model; needs M1 or later |
| Transcription languages | On Mac: 52 languages and dialects with the default model; 99 with Whisper | 10, including English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, and Chinese |
| Meeting notes | Recap, decisions, action items, and open questions, with citations back to the discussion | An Apple Intelligence summary of each recording |
| Where summaries run | On your Mac — llama.cpp built in; remote servers only if you approve them | Apple Intelligence, on your Mac or on Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers |
| Across meetings | Keyword and semantic search, cited answers, and a list of open action items | Each recording and its summary live in their own note |
| Where recordings are kept | A local library on your Mac; nothing syncs | In Notes — synced through iCloud if you use iCloud notes, end-to-end encrypted only with Advanced Data Protection |
| Dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | macOS Dictation, built in |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping: multi-word suggestions from a local model, in almost any app | Inline predictive text completes the word or phrase you're typing |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No — Screen Time shows time per app |
| Source code | Open source, GPLv3 | Proprietary |
| Price | Free | Free with macOS |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; Android companion app | Mac, iPhone, and iPad |

- **Q: Can't I record a Zoom call in Notes?** Only your side, unless the other voices reach your microphone through your speakers. Notes on macOS 27 requests microphone access only, so it can't capture another app's audio. LokalBot asks for both: the microphone for you, and macOS audio capture for the meeting app, so the other participants are recorded even through headphones. Either way, tell people you're recording.
- **Q: Are Apple Intelligence summaries private?** Apple designs them to be. Requests run on your Mac or on Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers, which Apple says don't keep your data. LokalBot's built-in summaries never leave your Mac, and its source code is public, so you can check. Notes stored in iCloud are end-to-end encrypted only if you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
- **Q: Does LokalBot replace Notes?** No. Keep Notes for notes, lists, and phone-call recordings. LokalBot is for meetings and recall: it records calls, writes notes you can trace back to the source, and exports them as Markdown when you want them elsewhere.

### LokalBot vs Otter (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-otter · verified 2026-10-26)

Otter is one of the best-known AI notetakers: its assistant joins Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet, transcribes in the cloud, and shares notes with your team. That reach comes with a participant in your call and your conversations on Otter's servers. LokalBot takes the opposite approach: it captures the call from your computer's own audio, transcribes and summarizes locally, and needs no account.

| Feature | LokalBot | Otter.ai |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How it captures a meeting | Microphone + system audio on your computer (just the selected app on Mac; on Windows and Linux, where it can be separated); source labels do not identify speakers | The Otter assistant joins Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet; its apps can also record directly |
| Where transcription runs | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR by default, with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | Otter's cloud |
| Account required | None | Yes |
| Works offline | After a one-time model download | Needs a connection |
| Transcription languages | On Mac: 52 languages and dialects with the default model; 99 with Whisper | English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, and Chinese |
| Free plan limits | None — the whole app is free | 300 transcription minutes per month |
| Team features | Single-user; share by exporting Markdown | Shared notes, team workspaces, and integrations |
| Connect AI tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | Otter MCP server |
| System-wide dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | No |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |
| Source code | Open source, GPLv3 | Proprietary |
| Price | Free | Basic free · Pro $16.99/mo, or $8.33/mo billed annually · Business $30/mo, or $19.99/mo billed annually · Enterprise custom |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; Android companion app | Web, Mac and Windows apps, iOS, Android, and a Chrome extension |

- **Q: Does LokalBot join my calls like Otter does?** No. Nothing joins the call and nothing appears in the participant list. LokalBot records your microphone and your computer's system audio, so it works with Zoom, Teams, Meet, Slack huddles, or any app that plays sound. You're still responsible for telling participants you're recording.
- **Q: Can I move my existing Otter.ai transcripts out?** Yes. LokalBot imports Otter.ai exports directly, or you can convert Otter transcripts into Obsidian Markdown locally in your browser with the free Meeting Migrator without uploading anything.
- **Q: Is on-device transcription accurate enough?** For most meetings, yes — but test it on your own audio. LokalBot defaults to Qwen3-ASR and lets you switch to Parakeet or Whisper in Settings, or to Granite Speech on Mac. The Local Desktop AI Leaderboard shows measured speed and word error rates against cloud STT APIs.
- **Q: What does LokalBot cost after the free tier?** There is no tier. LokalBot is free and open source under GPLv3, with no minute caps, no account, and no subscription.

### LokalBot vs Fireflies (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-fireflies · verified 2026-10-26)

Fireflies is built for teams: its notetaker joins your calls, transcribes in more than 100 languages, and pushes notes into CRMs and project tools. If your company runs on a shared call library, it's a strong choice. LokalBot is for the opposite need — notes that stay on your computer. It captures the call from your computer's audio with no bot, and runs transcription and summaries locally.

| Feature | LokalBot | Fireflies.ai |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How it captures a meeting | Mic + system audio on your computer — nothing joins the call | A notetaker joins Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, and more; the Mac and Windows desktop app and the Chrome extension can capture without it |
| Where transcription runs | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR by default, with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | Fireflies' cloud |
| Account required | None | Yes |
| Works offline | After a one-time model download | Needs a connection |
| Transcription languages | On Mac: 52 languages and dialects with the default model; 99 with Whisper | 100+ |
| Storage | Limited only by your disk | Free: 400 minutes per team · Pro: 8,000 minutes per seat · Business and up: unlimited |
| Integrations | A read-only CLI and MCP server; Markdown export and a daily memory note | CRMs, project tools, and an API |
| Compliance | No LokalBot server ever holds your meetings | HIPAA compliance and private storage on Enterprise |

- **Q: Why not use Fireflies without the bot?** You can capture without the bot through Fireflies' desktop app for Mac and Windows or its Chrome extension, but Fireflies still creates the transcript and summary and keeps them in its cloud, under your account. LokalBot keeps the audio, transcript, and summary on your computer.
- **Q: Can I migrate existing Fireflies transcripts?** Yes. LokalBot imports Fireflies exports into your local library, or you can convert them into plain Obsidian Markdown offline in your browser with the free Meeting Migrator.
- **Q: Can LokalBot push notes into my CRM?** Not directly. LokalBot exposes a read-only CLI and MCP server so local tools and agents can read your library, and it also exports meetings as Markdown and can write a daily memory note to a folder. Anything beyond that is up to you.
- **Q: Will people on the call know LokalBot is recording?** No — nothing appears in the call, which is why you need to tell participants yourself. On a fresh install, LokalBot asks through a notification before it records a detected meeting.

### LokalBot vs Fathom (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-fathom · verified 2026-11-20)

Fathom is popular for a reason: its free plan includes unlimited basic recordings and transcripts on Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams, and paid tiers add shared team folders and CRM sync for HubSpot and Salesforce. The trade-off is that your calls live in Fathom's cloud under an account, advanced AI summaries cap at five per month on the free tier, and most platforms still send a bot into the meeting. LokalBot captures from your computer's own audio with no bot, runs transcription and unlimited summaries locally, and needs no account.

- **Q: Can I bring my existing Fathom meetings into LokalBot?** Yes. LokalBot includes a built-in Fathom importer (transcripts, summaries, downloaded recordings, or Fathom API JSON), or you can convert Fathom exports into Obsidian Markdown offline in your browser with the free Meeting Migrator.
- **Q: Does Fathom work without a bot?** Fathom offers a bot-free capture option in beta on Mac, while Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams otherwise use the Fathom notetaker bot. Even without the bot, Fathom uploads and stores recordings and transcripts in its cloud. LokalBot processes audio, transcripts, and summaries locally by default.
- **Q: Why is LokalBot free when Fathom charges $15–$34 per seat?** LokalBot has no cloud transcription or LLM servers to pay for — the models run on your own Mac, Windows, or Linux computer. You pay for your own hardware and electricity, never a per-seat subscription.
- **Q: Will LokalBot work on apps besides Zoom, Meet, and Teams?** Yes. Because LokalBot captures local system audio rather than relying on platform bot APIs, it works with Slack huddles, Discord, Webex, FaceTime, WhatsApp, and any other call app on your computer.

### LokalBot vs Notion AI (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-notion-ai · verified 2026-11-20)

Notion AI Meeting Notes brings bot-free transcription right inside your workspace: type /meet in the Notion desktop app and your summary lands beside your team's docs and databases. The catch is that full access requires Notion's Business plan ($20/user/month billed annually for every workspace member), audio goes to cloud AI subprocessors (with zero data retention limited to Enterprise), and there is no Linux app. LokalBot gives you bot-free capture on your computer for free, runs speech and summary models locally, works offline, and exports clean Markdown anywhere.

| Feature | LokalBot | Notion AI Meeting Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where transcription and AI run | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR by default, with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | In the cloud via Notion and third-party AI subprocessors (such as OpenAI and Anthropic) |
| Account & workspace lock-in | None — local library plus plain Markdown export | Notion account required; notes live in your Notion workspace |
| Works offline | Fully, after a one-time model download | Needs a connection for AI transcription and summaries |
| Bot-free meeting capture | Microphone + system audio on your computer (just the selected app on Mac; on Windows and Linux, where it can be separated); labels show capture source, not identity | Bot-free in the Mac and Windows desktop apps (browser captures mic only) |
| Data retention & privacy | Audio, transcripts, and default summaries never leave your computer | No default model training; AI subprocessors may retain data up to 30 days on Business; zero retention requires Enterprise |
| Connect coding agents & tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | Notion AI connectors and API inside your workspace |
| System-wide dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | No |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |

- **Q: Can I still paste LokalBot summaries into Notion?** Yes. Open any meeting and choose Share → Copy as Markdown (or Export as Markdown), then paste straight into a Notion page — your audio and raw transcript still never touch a cloud server.
- **Q: Is Notion AI Meeting Notes included in Notion Free or Plus?** No. Notion folded full AI Meeting Notes into the Business ($20/user/month billed annually) and Enterprise tiers; Free and Plus accounts only receive a limited trial. LokalBot has no trial limits or per-seat pricing.
- **Q: Does Notion AI Meeting Notes run locally on my Mac?** No. While the Notion desktop app captures local system audio so no bot joins the call, it sends the audio to cloud AI subprocessors to transcribe and summarize. LokalBot runs both speech recognition and summarization on your own hardware by default.
- **Q: How does LokalBot compare for local AI coding agents?** LokalBot exposes a read-only local CLI and MCP server (off until enabled in Settings) so Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor can search your meetings and action items directly on your machine without cloud tokens or workspace permissions.

### LokalBot vs Read.ai (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-read-ai · verified 2026-11-20)

Read.ai connects to your calendar and dispatches the Read Assistant bot into Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet calls, adding engagement scores, coaching reports, and cross-tool search in its cloud. That bot-first model is also why many IT teams block Read.ai and why callers ask who invited the extra participant. LokalBot never joins a call, never emails attendees behind your back, runs transcription and summaries locally on your computer, and has no monthly meeting limit.

| Feature | LokalBot | Read.ai |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How it captures a meeting | Microphone + system audio on your computer — no bot ever enters the call or posts in meeting chat; labels show capture source, not identity | Read Assistant bot joins Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet as a visible participant and posts chat notices |
| Works when IT blocks meeting bots | Captures local audio directly — no external participant for hosts to admit or block | Blocked in many Zoom and Teams environments that restrict third-party bots |
| Where transcription and AI run | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR by default, with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | Read.ai's cloud |
| Account required | None | Yes |
| Works offline | Fully, after a one-time model download | Needs a connection |
| Free plan limits | Unlimited — the entire app is free | 5 meeting transcripts per month |
| Recording control | On a fresh install, asks via a local notification before recording; never auto-joins calendars | Calendar-connected bot can auto-join scheduled calls unless turned off per meeting or in settings |
| Compliance | No LokalBot server ever holds your meetings | HIPAA (BAA), SSO/SAML, and custom retention require Enterprise+ |
| System-wide dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | No |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping, in almost any app (on Linux: X11, or Wayland on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma) | No |
| Source code | Open source, GPLv3 | Proprietary |
| Price | Free | Free (5/mo) · Pro $15/mo annually ($19.75 monthly) · Enterprise $22.50/mo annually ($29.75 monthly) · Enterprise+ $29.75/mo annually ($39.75 monthly) |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; Android companion app | Cloud bot for Zoom, Teams, Meet; web, Slack, Outlook, iOS, and Android |

- **Q: Why do companies block Read.ai, and how is LokalBot different?** Most IT policies block third-party meeting bots because they join as an external cloud participant and upload confidential audio to outside servers. LokalBot runs on your computer with local models and no cloud backend — see our guide My company blocks AI notetaker bots for an IT review checklist. Always follow your organization's recording and consent rules.
- **Q: Will LokalBot ever auto-email meeting recaps to attendees?** No. LokalBot has no account, no email server, and no cloud sharing backend. Everything stays in your local library until you deliberately export or copy it.
- **Q: Does LokalBot cap how many meetings I can record per month?** No. Unlike Read.ai's 5-meeting free tier, LokalBot has no minute or meeting caps — storage is limited only by your own disk.
- **Q: How does speaker separation work without a bot?** LokalBot records your microphone and the meeting app's audio on separate tracks and runs local speaker diarization (Nemotron 3 Core ML on Mac, pyannote + TitaNet on Windows/Linux). Capture-track labels describe where audio came from rather than verified speaker identity, and you can name speakers locally.

### LokalBot vs Anarlog (Hyprnote) (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-hyprnote · verified 2026-11-20)

Hyprnote is the closest cousin on this list: open-source, local-first meeting notes — it helped prove the category. The app is now called anarlog, and hyprnote.com redirects to char.com, the team's newer product. The MIT-licensed anarlog app remains maintained, and it's good. Here's how LokalBot differs.

| Feature | LokalBot | Anarlog (Hyprnote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scope | Meetings, dictation, day timeline, autocomplete, and chat in one app | Meeting notetaker |
| Transcription | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR by default, with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | On-device models on supported Macs, or a cloud provider you select |
| Summaries and chat | llama.cpp built in — works with no keys and no setup | Your choice: a local server such as Ollama or LM Studio, your own API key, Apple Intelligence, or optional hosted AI |
| Cloud features | None — no account and no sync service; a remote inference server needs your approval | Opt-in hosted AI, encrypted CloudSync, and sharing |
| Notes on disk | Local SQLite library with full-text and vector search; Markdown export | Local SQLite plus plain files; Markdown export |
| Connect AI tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | Local CLI and MCP server |
| System-wide dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | No |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping, in almost any app (on Linux: X11, or Wayland on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma) | No |
| License | GPLv3 — every fork's improvements stay open | MIT for the community app; enterprise components are commercially licensed |
| Direction | Independent, local by default | Maintained as the community notetaker; the team now builds Char |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; Android companion app | macOS; Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android in beta |

- **Q: Aren't you basically the same project?** We overlap on the part that matters — local, bot-free meeting notes — and that's a good thing; the category needs more of it. We differ on scope (a workspace vs a notetaker), on shipped local AI vs bring-your-own model, and on license.
- **Q: What's Char?** The team's current product: an AI notepad in private beta at char.com, backed by Y Combinator. It's a separate codebase from the open-source anarlog app, which the team says remains maintained.
- **Q: Why GPLv3 instead of MIT?** Copyleft. Anyone can fork LokalBot, but improvements have to stay open. For an app that hears your meetings and reads your screen, we want the audit path to survive every fork — the code you can read should always be the code you run.

### LokalBot vs Meetily (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-meetily · verified 2026-10-26)

Meetily is one of the most popular open-source meeting notetakers, with a large community behind it. Like LokalBot, it records your microphone and system audio without a bot, transcribes on your device, and can write summaries with a built-in local model. Its free Community Edition is MIT-licensed and runs on macOS and Windows. A paid Pro edition, built on a separate codebase, adds speaker separation, meeting detection, and AI-tool connections. LokalBot ships every feature in one free GPLv3 app, and covers more of your workday than meetings.

| Feature | LokalBot | Meetily |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meeting capture | Bot-free microphone + system audio; detects meetings and, on a fresh install, asks before recording | Bot-free microphone + system audio; automatic meeting detection is Pro only |
| Transcription | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR by default, with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | On your device — Whisper or Parakeet |
| Summaries | llama.cpp built in — works with no keys and no setup | Built-in Qwen 3.5 models, Ollama, or your own Claude, OpenAI, Groq, or OpenRouter key |
| Speaker separation | On your computer, on by default | Pro only |
| Ask across meetings | Cited answers that link back to the transcript and audio | Not yet — listed as coming soon for Pro |
| Connect AI tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | Pro only — MCP, webhooks, and a CLI |
| Transcribe existing files | Import audio and video recordings as meetings | Imports audio and video files, and can re-transcribe them |
| Usage analytics | None — no analytics service or telemetry | Optional; off by default on new installs |
| System-wide dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | No |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping, in almost any app (on Linux: X11, or Wayland on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma) | No |
| License | GPLv3 — every feature in one open repository | Community: MIT · Pro: a separate commercial codebase |
| Price | Free | Community free · Pro $10 per user/mo, billed annually · Enterprise custom |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; Android companion app | macOS on Apple Silicon and Windows; Linux builds from source |

- **Q: Isn't Meetily also free and open source?** Its Community Edition is, under the MIT license, and it does the core job well: bot-free capture, on-device transcription, and local summaries. Speaker separation, automatic meeting detection, advanced exports, and MCP access are in Meetily Pro, a paid edition built on a separate codebase. LokalBot keeps everything in one open repository, and all of it is free.
- **Q: Do they use the same models?** Partly. Both can transcribe with Parakeet or Whisper, and both offer Qwen 3.5 for local summaries. LokalBot defaults to Qwen3-ASR for transcription and also offers Granite Speech on Mac; the benchmarks page compares several of these models on the same test set, measured on a Mac.
- **Q: Which one runs on Windows?** Both. The Meetily Community Edition runs on macOS and Windows. LokalBot runs on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later, and its Windows 10/11 and Linux apps are in alpha, with a few Mac features still missing. The system requirements page covers each platform.

OpenWhispr is a popular open-source app for dictation and meeting notes, under the MIT license. Like LokalBot, it records your microphone and system audio without a bot and can transcribe and summarize on your device. Its setup recommends OpenWhispr Cloud, though, and device sync, its MCP server, and team features come with paid plans. LokalBot runs on your computer by default, keeps every feature free in one GPLv3 app, and remembers more of your workday than meetings.

| Feature | LokalBot | OpenWhispr |

| Transcription | On your computer — Qwen3-ASR by default, with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | On your device with Orukeet (a Parakeet fine-tune), Whisper, and others, or cloud providers |
| Summaries | llama.cpp built in — works with no keys and no setup | Built-in llama.cpp models, a local server such as Ollama, your own keys, or OpenWhispr Cloud |
| Speaker separation | On your computer, on by default; names carry into later meetings | On your device, up to 8 speakers; names carry into later meetings |
| Ask across meetings | Cited answers that link back to the transcript and audio | A chat agent that searches, reads, and edits your notes |
| Connect AI tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | A hosted MCP server on paid plans that sees notes synced to its cloud; a local CLI for free |
| Transcribe existing files | Import audio and video recordings as meetings | Files, batch uploads, and YouTube links |
| System-wide dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | Hotkeys for dictation, a voice assistant, translation, and meetings |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping, in almost any app (on Linux: X11, or Wayland on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma) | No |
